examples.text: The governor just gave me a rise of two pound six.

glosses: The amount of material extending from waist to crotch in a pair of trousers or shorts.

examples.text: The rise of his pants was so low that his tailbone was exposed.

glosses: The front of a diaper.
A small hill; used chiefly in place names.
An area of terrain that tends upward away from the viewer, such that it conceals the region behind it; a slope.

examples.text: the land rolls gently, so that, upon cresting a low rise or passing a copse of wind turbines, you suddenly spot a lot full of lorries or a complex of gigantic sheds.
I went along up the bank with one eye out for pap and t'other one out for what the rise might fetch along.

glosses: A very noticeable visible or audible reaction of a person or group.

examples.text: Making fun of their football team is one sure way to get a rise from a crowd.
She really got a rise from the audience when she donned a wig and talked like the president.

glosses: The height of an arch or a step.

examples.text: As the rise, i.e. height, of the arch decreases, the outward thrust increases.
Each step had a rise of 170 mm and a going of 250 mm.

glosses: Alternative form of rice (“twig”).
The stock of a family; a race or generation of progenitors.

examples.text: Where ye may all that are of noble ſtemm / Approach, and kiſs her ſacred veſtures hemm.
While I do pray, learn here thy stem / And true descent.

glosses: A branch of a family.

examples.text: This is a stem / Of that victorious stock.

glosses: A branch of a family.
A branch, or group of branches, located outside a family or other cladistic group, but which is more closely related to that group than to any other taxon of the same rank.
An advanced or leading position; the lookout.

examples.text: Wolsey sat at the stem more than twenty years.

glosses: The above-ground stalk (technically axis) of a vascular plant, and certain anatomically similar, below-ground organs such as rhizomes, bulbs, tubers, and corms.

examples.text: After they are shot up thirty feet in length, they spread a very large top, having no bough nor twig in the trunk or the stem.
He had placed her upon the grass by now, her back resting against the stem of a huge tree. At her question he stepped back where he could the better see her face.

glosses: A slender supporting member of an individual part of a plant such as a flower or a leaf; also, by analogy, the shaft of a feather.

examples.text: the stem of an apple or a cherry

Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close (less than half a meter) above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them.

glosses: A narrow part on certain man-made objects, such as a wine glass, a tobacco pipe, a spoon.

The main part of an uninflected word to which affixes may be added to form inflections of the word. A stem often has a more fundamental root. Systematic conjugations and declensions derive from their stems.

examples.text: The praenomen and nomen for the most part consisted of simple stems with the suffix -us or -ius, which correspond to some of the contracted forms in other languages […].

glosses: A person's leg.

examples.text: She was perfectly, fuckably proportioned everywhere else, both above and below her waist. A pocket-size Venus, with the longest stems he'd ever seen on someone so dang diminutive.

glosses: The penis.

examples.text: Waves of ecstasy roll through him as the moustachioed Casanova slides his stem in and out of the spaced-out chick.

glosses: A vertical stroke of a letter.
A vertical stroke marking the length of a note in written music.
A premixed portion of a track for use in audio mastering and remixing.

examples.text: Stem mastering processes a mix by breaking it down into several manageable pieces—that is, stereo stems. The stem approach allows the mastering engineer the opportunity to make larger or smaller changes to separate mix elements before the final compression and limiting are applied to the complete mix.

glosses: The vertical or nearly vertical forward extension of the keel, to which the forward ends of the planks or strakes are attached.
The front part of a vessel.

examples.text: from stem to stern

Both we will walke vpon the loftie cliffes,
And Chriſtian Merchants that with Ruſſian ſtems
Plow vp huge furrowes in the Caſpian ſea,
Shall vaile to vs, as Lords of al the Lake.

glosses: A component on a bicycle that connects the handlebars to the bicycle fork.
A part of an anatomic structure considered without its possible branches or ramifications.
A crack pipe; or the long, hollow portion of a similar pipe (i.e. meth pipe) resembling a crack pipe.
A winder on a clock, watch, or similar mechanism.
To remove the stem from.

examples.text: to stem cherries; to stem tobacco leaves

glosses: To be caused or derived; to originate.

examples.text: The current crisis stems from the short-sighted politics of the previous government.
Weight stigma often stems from an idea that patients are at fault for their body size.

glosses: To descend in a family line.
To direct the stem (of a ship) against; to make headway against.

examples.text: Nor is the pre-eminent tremendousness of the great Sperm Whale anywhere more feelingly comprehended, than on board of those prows which stem him.

glosses: To hit with the stem of a ship; to ram.

examples.text: As when two warlike Brigandines at sea, / With murdrous weapons arm'd to cruell fight, / Doe meete together on the watry lea, / They stemme ech other with so fell despight, / That with the shocke of their owne heedlesse might, / Their wooden ribs are shaken nigh a sonder […]

glosses: To ram (clay, etc.) into a blasting hole.
To stop, hinder (for instance, a river or blood).

examples.text: to stem a tide
[They] stem the flood with their erected breasts.
Stemm'd the wild torrent of a barbarous age.

glosses: To move the feet apart and point the tips of the skis inward in order to slow down the speed or to facilitate a turn.
In rock climbing, to use a stance with the feet spread apart, bracing them in opposite directions against the two walls of a chimney or dihedral.
Alternative form of steem.
Alternative form of STEM.

examples.text: Stem (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) fields are a particular cause for concern because within them there are more pronounced stereotypes, extreme competitiveness and gender inequities regarding the abilities and competencies of black male and female students.

glosses: Alternative spelling of stemme (“lesbian who combines stud and femme traits”).
To be much taller or higher than something; to loom over.

examples.text: It is this stretch which provides what is perhaps the most staggering scenic prospect of all; the impression made on the mind by the overwhelming height of the Eiger, towering over the train, is almost impossible to describe.

glosses: To be much greater or more important than.

examples.text: There are three phyla of worms that, in terms of diversity and abundance, tower over the rest: the Roundworms (nematodes), the Annelids and the Flatworms.
